lines: A village... though it's nothing but ruins...
Fuuma felt a slight discomfort watching Kagero gaze forward, as if expecting something.
But why do you want to go to a place like that?
Why... heh, I do not know myself. It is just...
It is nothing... I simply hope to find some kind of clue. That is all.
Kagero forced down the breath that had risen to the tip of her vocal cords, masking it with a faint smile.
I see... I hope we find some kind of clue...
Heh, Fuuma Kotaro. There is no point in staying here any longer. Let us go quickly.
From then on, until they crossed the pass, only the sound of two pairs of feet treading on grass and the calls of birds echoed quietly.
That is the Koukawa Village we are looking for.
As Fuuma pointed to the village spreading out below them, Kagero hurriedly ran two or three steps forward.
As you can see, it's a ruin, right?
Looking at the cluster of dilapidated houses, which were clearly abandoned even from the pass, Fuuma took a deep breath into his chest.
Finally seeing the destination, Kagero held her breath and stared straight ahead.
Watching her slender, fragile shoulders tremble with fear, Fuuma had no words to offer her,
and could only stare at Koukawa Village over Kagero's shoulder.
...Staying here any longer will accomplish nothing...
Fuuma Kotaro, let us go to the village.
Fuuma led the way down into the village, watching Kagero smile as if she were suppressing her emotions.
Once they arrived in the village, they had no specific purpose and wandered aimlessly through the streets.
Why did you want to come here?
I do not know myself. But... if I come here, something...
She had visited the ruins of Koukawa Village to search for a connection to the world she had once lived in.
Fuuma could read that kind of thought in her expression, so he deliberately chose not to pry any further.
She looked at the decaying houses, felt the scent of earth and the refreshing breeze in the overgrown fields that had once been farmland,
and, as if sending her thoughts to the people who had once lived their lives here, Kagero occasionally closed her eyes and prayed.
Many people must have lived and died here once too...
Kagero bit her lip, thinking of the fate of the people who had lived and died here long ago.
Fuuma could only watch as Kagero closed her eyes tightly, as if rejecting everything.
Seeing Kagero project her own future onto Koukawa Village, Fuuma felt sorry for her, but still opened his mouth.
I probably shouldn't say this, but...
I don't think this village... this era... necessarily has to be the same as what lies ahead in your world...
So please... don't... don't make that pained face...
Kagero, who had snapped out of her daze at Fuuma's words, smiled gently, sensing his feelings.
Kotaro... you are so kind... hehe~
The era and world in which she lived were not necessarily connected to the future of Kagero's world.
Kagero briefly looked surprised at Fuuma's comforting words, but her expression quickly softened again.
It's not necessarily the same as what lies ahead in my world...
Kagero crouched down, murmuring softly as if chewing over Fuuma's words.
Kotaro, please look. What lovely flowers...
She gently gathered the small flowers blooming quietly by the roadside and held them softly against her chest.
Fuuma was left speechless by the beauty of Kagero's melancholic profile.
Flowers that bloom anywhere... I see... perhaps you are right...
But... that is what makes them beautiful...
Gazing at the flowers, she broke into a fleeting smile, then gently cradled the delicate blossoms and rose to her feet again.
Kotaro... let us look around a little longer.
Seeing Kagero's expression soften into a calm one, Fuuma felt a sense of relief. He followed her as they walked through the village once more, and then
the two of them headed toward a small hill from which the entire village could be seen.
Kotaro... the village of Koukawa looks truly beautiful from up here.
A gentle breeze caressed Kagero's soft skin, lightly lifting her beautiful, silk-like hair.
May I pay my respects to the people of Koukawa who lived here?
Kagero knelt on the spot and quietly gathered stones, piling them up one by one with delicate, careful hands.
I am making a memorial stele. It will not take long. Please forgive my taking this liberty.
That is not a problem, but...
Kagero continued to pile up the stones steadily, not caring that her high-quality kimono or her slender, beautiful fingers were getting dirty with the soil.
Will you not let me help you?
Unable to bear watching her get covered in dirt, Fuuma pleaded for the chance to help.
I appreciate the offer, but there is no need for someone from another clan to touch it.
Rejected and unable to do anything, Fuuma stood there as Kagero continued.
Besides, this is something I must do alone, as one who was left behind.
Fuuma looked embarrassed, staring at the stones being piled up by Kagero's hands, and waited quietly for the stele to be completed.
With each stone she placed, Kagero's lips trembled slightly as she murmured something.
The tiny sound, neither a sigh nor a voice, was swallowed by the soft, gentle wind and never reached Fuuma's ears.
I wondered what Kagero was thinking as she stacked the stones, or whom she was mourning.
I was curious, but Fuuma knew he was not permitted to ask, so he waited in silence for the monument to be completed.
Kotaro-sama... I apologize for the wait.
Without asking Fuuma for any help at all, Kagero had built the memorial monument entirely on her own.
This is... quite a fine monument.
Please, do not flatter me. It is a simple monument made from whatever stones were available...
Though small, the stone monument was perfectly balanced. Fuuma let out an involuntary exclamation of admiration, to which Kagero replied with humility.
The monument is complete, but there is still...
The solidly constructed stone monument stood strong and dignified, much like Kagero herself.
Kagero knelt before the monument she had erected and offered the small flower she had picked earlier.
That was a flower for mourning, wasn't it?
Indeed it was. It pains me that I can only offer something so modest...
Kagero watched the flower offered to the simple monument sway gently in the wind, seeing her own reflection in the scene.
Does the size of the offering matter for a mourning? Isn't the sentiment behind it what truly counts?
Seeing the tension in her expression ease slightly, Fuuma let out a small breath of relief.
May I join you in mourning as well?
If Kotaro-sama so wishes, I have no reason to stop you.
Fuuma knelt beside Kagero, staring intently at the small flower and the small monument.
Kagero pressed her hands together and bowed her head slightly, weaving words of condolence that never reached Fuuma's ears, carried away and lost to the wind.
Following her example, Fuuma faced the monument and pressed his hands together, expressing his condolences for those who had died in the village.
After a gentle wind, as if carrying the thoughts of the mourned, flowed past, the two of them, hands clasped, were enveloped in silence.
Kotaro-sama... just now, you mentioned that this place might be different from the village of the Koga Man'yoku Shu.
Gazing at the monument he had erected with his own eyes, Kagero opened her mouth slightly and began to weave her words.
I have walked this place, and I came to feel that Kotaro-sama's words may indeed be true.
If that is the case... then there was no need to make a monument like this.
Having felt that this was a world separate from his own, Fuuma asked if there was really any need to dirty his kimono just to build a monument. She shook her head slightly.
However, even so... even if those who completed their lives here were from another world or were people of the future...
I wish to mourn them... I must mourn them...
Fuuma was left speechless by her quiet yet somehow powerful words and voice.
As a Koga... I wish to mourn the lives of the Koukawa people, who may have been my kin...
I am kind...? Fufu... that is not the case.
Seeing Kagero's softly smiling profile and the way she pressed her hands together for people whose identities were unknown, Fuuma was painfully reminded of the depth of her emotions.
The wind, which had been gently rustling until then, suddenly blew strongly, as if trying to wipe something away.
The merciless wind scattered the petals of the flowers Kagero had carefully offered, making them fall in a fleeting manner.
While Fuuma reached out his hand to prevent the flowers from becoming a mess, Kagero simply watched the scene unfold.
Hey...! If this continues, the flowers will all scatter. Aren't you going to do anything about it?
The petals swaying in the wind were on the verge of crumbling, barely holding together.
Fuuma was anxious, fearing that if he didn't take action, the offering he had prepared would be ruined.
Kotaro-sama... it is fine as it is.
While Fuuma struggled to calm himself and contain the situation, Kagero spoke in a composed manner.
All things are impermanent... everything will eventually, like this flower...
...and fade away, destined to scatter like this village...
Before Kagero, who spoke quietly, the petals swayed silently, trembling in the air.
Even as Fuuma listened to Kagero's words, he couldn't help but worry about the petals that seemed ready to fall at any moment.
Though it is a sorrowful thing... it is not merely a parting...
It may also be the liberation of the soul, to meet again beyond the barriers of this life...
The liberation of the soul, to meet again...
The moment Kagero finished speaking, all the petals were caught by the wind and vanished into the distance.
I feel like I understand now.
The wind that had scattered all the petals stopped as if its duty was done, and peace returned to the hill.
Kagero did not ask what Fuuma had understood.
There was no need to ask.
(So that's it... it really is that different...)
He remembered how each word she wove felt as if it were piercing deep into his heart.
(Even though we are both ninja... we are completely different beings...)
The words spoken by a woman who had lived in a world of life and death were incredibly heavy,
and Fuuma's mind kept replaying her words, layering them over and over.
Come, let us go, Fuuma Kotaro.
After finishing the rites and standing up, brushing the dirt from her kimono, she smiled gently at Fuuma.
Fuuma Kotaro... is something the matter?
At the sound of Kagero's soft voice, his brain, which had been frozen, began to move again.
So... where do you want to go next?
I have finished paying my respects, so there is nothing left for me to regret in this place.
The faint darkness he had felt when they first arrived in this village was no longer visible on her face now that the rites were complete.
I see. Then let's head back to the mansion.
A ninja who had lived within the chains of the past.
Though she was a ninja just like him, a human just like him, the core of her being was that of a different kind of creature.
Confronted so starkly with her view of life and death, Fuuma felt the gulf between himself and Kagero more vividly than ever.
